A scratch page for tuning the data center jitter. Each map exposes two live
controls (below the chart):

- **Jitter on** — checkbox to toggle the overlap-spreading on/off, so you can
  A/B the raw stacked marks against the jittered ones.
- **Jitter amount (°)** — slider for the spread in degrees. The current baked
  default is `charts.overlay.JITTER_SPREAD`; once you settle on a value, set that
  constant (in `charts/overlay.py`) to make it the default everywhere.

The controls scale each mark's precomputed spiral offset in the browser, so
they respond instantly without re-running Python.

**Which marks move** is decided in pandas by proximity clustering: marks within
`charts.overlay.CLUSTER_DIST` degrees of each other (single linkage) form a
cluster and fan apart; the largest mark in each cluster stays anchored at its
true spot. `CLUSTER_DIST = 0` would separate only exact ZIP-centroid collisions;
the current value also splits nearby-but-distinct metro sites (Ashburn, San
Antonio, Columbus…) whose big marks overlap. Because clustering runs in Python,
changing `CLUSTER_DIST` needs a **re-render** — it is not a live slider.

> This page is intentionally **not** in the `_quarto.yml` render list, so it does
> not ship to the deployed dashboard. Render it on its own with
> `quarto render jitter-lab.qmd`.

```{python}
#| include: false
#| label: setup
import charts

charts.setup()
```

## Baseline water stress (sized by power)

```{python}
#| echo: false
charts.interactive(charts.water.baseline_stress_with_datacenters(controls=True))
```
